I farm only 3.5 mu, and I have been doing wheat-maize rotation for many years, so I will keep the whole 3.5 mu in that system. Because my land is small, my household labor is limited, and some family members work off-farm, I will keep things simple and steady rather than take risks. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield at the key stages, but I still want to control costs because the farm is small. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer up front with enough nitrogen for stable tillering and grain filling, and irrigate a few times because wheat in my area depends on water for a good harvest. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed because that is what I would trust for stronger yield on such a small plot, then I will fertilize a bit heavier on nitrogen than wheat and give a couple of irrigations if rainfall is not enough. I will use rotary tillage because it fits a small farm like mine and keeps the work manageable. I will spray only as needed but I still expect a few pesticide applications over the year because I do not want weeds, insects, or disease to cut yield on limited land.
